J2 calibration · kill test · 31 cells · 279 judge calls

What the judge actually watched

Every clip scored in the J2 sweep, playable, with the θ that produced it and the score it drew. Watching them changes the conclusion: the kill test failed because the clips do not depict fabric. The judge was never shown the information it was asked for.

correction to the J2 report

The FAIL stands — the numbers below are unchanged. What was wrong was the attribution. It was reported as the judge being unable to read material character. On inspection the cloth renders as a near-uniform dark silhouette covering 4–6% of the frame, with an interquartile range of two grey levels. There is no fold, drape or sheen cue in the pixels at all. Gross outline motion is the only channel that survives, which is exactly what the judge scored on.

The verdict it produced

Pass required AUC ≥ 0.70 and Spearman > 0.25 — correct-region clips outranking wrong-material clips. AUC 0.5 is chance.

The cause, and the fix

J0 chose environment="default" over "studio" because measured cloth-against-background contrast was 80/255 versus 39/255. That measured the silhouette edge — and optimising it picked the lighting that flattens the interior. Swapping to studio lighting and framing the cloth to fill the shot restores shading: folds and creases become visible, and silk stops looking like tarp. normals, color, roughness and metallic on log_mesh were tested and produce byte-identical pixels — lighting and framing are the levers that work.

light silk default / wide cloth IQR 38-39 · sd 6.76 · 10% of frame
light silk studio / close cloth IQR 22-32 · sd 7.60 · 41% of frame
stiff plastic tarp default / wide cloth IQR 39-39 · sd 6.72 · 10% of frame
stiff plastic tarp studio / close cloth IQR 22-23 · sd 3.12 · 50% of frame

The right-hand frames are the tell. Under studio light silk buckles into a visible crease (cloth grey spread 22–32) while the tarp stays smooth (22–23). Under the old render both sit at 38–39 — the two materials were pixel-wise indistinguishable, so no judge, however good, could have separated them.

The literal model input

The mp4s are 91 frames at 30 fps, but CosmosJudge._decode subsamples to 4 fps — so the model receives 12 frames. These strips are that exact decode, reproduced by the same code path. Compare the two: the one the judge liked moves further across the strip.
